Name: neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run
Structural Path: debug_ctrl.run -> debug execution control -> privilege-control path -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Mechanisms: For a load or store issued while `mstatus_mprv = 1`, the control unit assigns `ctrl_o.lsu_priv <= csr.mstatus_mpp`. `neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run` can alter the CSR write, trap/debug return, or stored `mstatus_mpp` value used by that MPRV branch; the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run`, `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv`. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. The supporting RTL chain is `neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. The LSU request metadata carries an unintended effective privilege, allowing a memory access to be checked as a more privileged operation.

The assignment `lsu_priv <= mstatus_mpp when mstatus_mprv = '1' else prv_level` makes `mstatus_mprv` the privilege-source selector. `neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run` reaches that selector or one of its CSR update controls; the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run`, `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv`. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. The supporting RTL chain is `neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. The LSU selects the wrong privilege source and applies an unintended protection domain to the pending memory request.
Justification: A false debug-run state changes the privilege/control context and showed the strongest authorization-bypass response.
